cells.tense: Right now you have the pen, and you're using it to pick what to tend.
cells.ask: Mark one thing you already do daily for someone as care rather than chore, and keep doing it the same way this week.
cells.core:
You're picking what gets your care, and you know you're picking. You tend the person, the project, the thing small or unfinished. There's a direction in it. You can say 'this one, now' and mean it, and it shows in what you water and what you leave alone. The growing thing keeps its own schedule, and you've been letting it.

The balance holds while the direction stays clear and you stay off the clock of the thing you tend. When it slips, picking turns into pushing, and the work gets smaller for it. The ask is to mark one thing you already do daily for someone as care rather than chore, and keep doing it the same way this week. Keeping the balance means you tend without asking the growing thing to say thank you.
cells.sheetLine: You pick what gets your care, and the care works because you picked.
cells.verb: choosing a direction and meaning it
cells.place: where something is growing and needs tending

cells.tense: You are forward in your head to a future where it has already worked out.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're steering and leave it untouched for a week — no adjusting, no reworking, no measuring to see if it moved.
cells.core:
You've gone past tending into steering. Ahead of you there's a picture of how the growing thing should look, and you're holding to that picture instead of the thing itself. So you nudge, adjust, prepare for what hasn't happened. You check progress on a schedule the thing didn't agree to.

What that does is press the outcome and skip its own timing. Nothing can grow on the pace you're setting. The ask is to take one thing you're steering and leave it alone for a week — no adjusting, no reworking, no measuring it to see if it moved. Then you'll see what it does on its own, and what your hands were doing to it.

cells.tense: You're still stopped at a door you already walked through, and it's holding the pen.
cells.ask: Choose one small thing that gets watered today — a plant, a person's message, a project page — and tend it for ten minutes without asking what good it does.
cells.core:
Direction feels like something other people have. You've watched things you cared for go wrong, or ask too much, or not notice, and somewhere in that you stopped picking what gets tended. Now care happens on its own, for whatever comes, because picking seems like it will only fail again. So you wait for purpose to arrive, and it doesn't.

The ability isn't gone; it's unexercised. The way back is small and specific. The ask is to choose one small thing that gets watered today — a plant, a person's message, a project page — and tend it for ten minutes without asking what good it does. You're not trying to feel driven. You're putting your hands back on one thing you chose.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped picking what to tend, and now nothing seems to need you.

cells.tense: You're already directing what happens next, but you're explaining it as just how things go.
cells.ask: Say out loud the one thing your steady care is keeping alive right now, and that you're the one keeping it alive.
cells.core:
You are shaping what happens for people around you — what you take on, what you let be, what you show up for. But your own account doesn't include that. You say the work has a life of its own, or the person just needs more, or this is simply what you do. You've been picking what gets tended, and the picking hasn't been called yours.

The direction is running. It's just not claimed. The ask is to say out loud the one thing your steady care is keeping alive right now, and that you're the one keeping it alive. Not to take credit for gain. To put your name back on a choice that's already been made — and then see how it changes what you keep choosing.
cells.sheetLine: You're already deciding what gets cared for. The deciding isn't owned.
